note.note:
ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • “Not having much of an appetite and energy lately”; no food, medication, or environmental trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Loss of appetite ≈ 3.5 months (after changing jobs).  
  • Unintentional weight loss ≈ 1 stone (~6 kg) over ≈ 6 months.  
  • Fatigue/low energy over “months.”  
  • Episodic palpitations + perceived breathlessness specifically in elevators (each episode self-limited); onset timeframe not precisely stated.  
  • Occasional nausea; no vomiting.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: not reported.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: not reported.  
  • Drooling: not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: not reported.  
  • Dyspnea: only transient in elevators; able to walk a mile without dyspnea (has been generally sedentary).  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: not reported.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: not reported.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar ENT or allergic episodes.  
  • No ED visits, epinephrine use, or airway interventions ever reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food/environmental allergies: not documented.  
  • Medications: Previously on levothyroxine; stopped “months ago.” No current prescription or OTC medications documented.
- Social context:
  • 35-year-old male lawyer; reports job-related stress.  No comment on accompaniment/supervision at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none reported via tele-visit.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor; normal speech; episodic subjective breathlessness only in lifts.
- Mental status: alert, coherent; mood described as “down.”
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (video consultation only).
- Presence of another person with patient: not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression: Constitutional symptoms (fatigue, appetite loss, unintentional weight loss) with situational palpitations; no evidence of acute ENT/allergic pathology.
  Evidence: gradual onset, absence of airway symptoms, normal bowels, episodic elevator-related palpitations, history of untreated hypothyroidism, low mood.
- DDx reference (top aligned items):
  1. Major depressive disorder – low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue; temporally linked to job change.
  2. Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism – history of primary hypothyroidism; stopped levothyroxine; fatigue and low mood consistent (opposing evidence: weight loss rather than gain, palpitations atypical).
  3. Iron-deficiency or other anaemia – could explain fatigue, headaches, occasional dyspnea; requires labs for confirmation.
  (All above consistent with transcript; no ENT-specific differential identified.)
- No conflicting ENT findings; no acute airway threat.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • None required from ENT standpoint; no airway compromise.
- Investigations ordered/advised:
  • Comprehensive blood panel (CBC, U&E, LFTs, thyroid profile, iron studies, vitamin B12/folate) as arranged by primary clinician.
- Patient instructions:
  • Arrange blood draw via support number in app; book follow-up once results available.  
  • Seek emergency care (call 999/A&E) for new chest pain, persistent or worsening breathlessness, throat tightness, voice change, sudden facial/oral swelling, or syncope.
- Follow-up:
  • Review blood results; consider endocrinology referral if thyroid dysfunction confirmed.  
  • Consider mental-health assessment if depression suspected.  
  • Reinforce medication adherence once thyroid status clarified.  
  • No ENT follow-up needed unless new airway or otolaryngologic symptoms develop.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, full allergy list, medication dose/route/frequency, review of night sweats/fever, ENT physical exam, availability of emergency medications (e.g., auto-injector not applicable but not asked), smoking/alcohol history.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none identified.
● Transcript quality: clear audio; occasional overlapping speech but key clinical details audible.
